title: The Bullet Holes That Fooled The Generals
sources: EXAMPLE ONLY: dramatized scenes; re-check every fact with 2 fresh sources before publishing
Wikipedia, 'Survivorship bias' (Abraham Wald and the returning WWII bombers)
Mangel & Samaniego, 'Abraham Wald's Work on Aircraft Survivability', Journal of the American Statistical Association 79 (1984)

lines.text: Nineteen forty-three. Bombers limp back to the runway, wings and tails shredded.
The general slams the table. "Bolt armor on every spot that got hit!"
But armor is heavy, and a heavy bomber climbs slowly and burns more fuel.
Then a quiet mathematician, Abraham Wald, walks in and stares at the same planes.
"Sir, you are only counting the planes that made it back."
"So where are the bombers that never landed?"
Nobody in the war room says a word.
Picture judging a diner only by the people who walk out smiling.
You never hear from the guy who went home with food poisoning.
Wald points at the engines on the returning planes. Barely a scratch.
"Planes hit here never came home. This is where the armor goes."
The general hesitates, because one wrong guess costs real crews.
Wald's idea flips the whole plan: protect the clean spots.
The missing planes were the real evidence all along.
So next time you only see the winners, remember that sometimes
